# Practitioner Academy Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy | 2 days, live virtual | US$12,500

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client is at the piloting stage of AI maturity and has three AI use cases:

- **Customer service chatbot:** deployed on the support portal.
- **AI visual inspection:** in pilot on the German production line.
- **AI sales forecasting:** planned for next year.

The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The owner of that finding's remediation is Unknown.

Your stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Client also intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although the start date is not fixed.

The Client names ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. Whether existing registers, procedures or records under those frameworks can host AI governance content is Unknown and will be confirmed with participants rather than assumed.

## 2. Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The window between a decision by 15 December 2026 and a Q2 2027 production date is short. Governance written by outsiders and handed over tends to stall when the people who must run it have not built it. The Practitioner Academy closes that gap. Your own practitioners work directly in two open frameworks and leave with started artifacts they own and can continue unaided:

- **GRC Workbook:** https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook
- **Slow AI Kitchen:** https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen

The program also answers the June 2026 audit finding in the most concrete way available: Day 1 produces a started AI system inventory. The program is anchored in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

The Profile names the following audience roles for the two days:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

## 3. Worked Examples

Two use cases run as the worked examples across both days.

- **AI visual inspection (pilot).** This use case is the subject of your Q2 2027 objective. It also carries the works council constraint, so it is the best test of whether governance can gate a production release.
- **Customer service chatbot (deployed).** This is the only system already live. It carries the EU customer data constraint and GDPR exposure, so it tests governance of a running system rather than a planned one.

Sales forecasting enters the inventory as a planned system. Because it is not yet built, it is not carried through the full exercise set.

## 4. Two-Day Curriculum

Each day runs as four 90-minute working sessions. Module and pattern names follow the curriculum spine. File-level paths are issued in pre-work.

**Day 1: GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)

| Session | Exercise | Module | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *The Turtle and the Phoenix* told from the [facilitation kit](https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md) to seat the doctrine before the instruments arrive on Day 2. The kit's handle map is used as the bridge to the workbook modules. Participants then sketch who decides what for AI at Tamarack. The session closes with the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise. | Governance structures | Draft roles and decision-rights map, with unassigned owners marked Unknown |
| 2 | Record the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting systems with their deployment states as stated. Draft a working EU AI Act classification for Legal review. This is not a legal determination. | AI system inventories and classification | Started AI system inventory (three entries) |
| 3 | Assess risks and impacts for the visual inspection pilot and for the chatbot's EU data residency requirement. | Risk and impact assessments | Draft risk register entries for both systems |
| 4 | Draft a production-release procedure for visual inspection. Works council consultation is written in as a precondition. | Policies and operating procedures | Draft operating procedure (release gate) |

**Day 2: Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) **plus assurance**

| Session | Exercise | Pattern | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Govern the chatbot's instructions using fictional support tickets. | Governed prompting | Governed prompt record |
| 6 | Design two workflows: chatbot escalation to a human agent, and human disposition of visual inspection rejects. | Practical AI workflow design | Two governed workflow specifications |
| 7 | Assign accountable roles at each decision point in both workflows. | Human oversight and accountability | Oversight and accountability matrix |
| 8 | Build the evidence trail for the inventory and both workflows, set acceptance criteria using The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done) and outline board reporting using AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). | Evidence collection and audit readiness | Evidence map and draft acceptance checklist |

## 5. Constraint Handling

- **Customer data must stay in the EU.** No real customer data or transcripts are used. Chatbot exercises run on fictional support tickets.
- **Works council consultation before anything touches production staff.** Visual inspection exercises use a sanitized analog with fictional defect records. No production staff data or imagery is used. Every visual inspection artifact is a draft. Any workflow affecting production staff is flagged for works council consultation before adoption.

## 6. Deliverables

Participants leave with the following started artifacts, all held in the Client's working copies of the repositories:

- A started AI system inventory
- Draft risk register entries
- At least two governed workflows
- A draft release-gate procedure
- An oversight matrix
- An evidence map

These artifacts can inform later ISO/IEC 42001 work. No certification or audit outcome is promised.
